The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VOS appliance and is not required after provisioning is complete. CVE-2026-99187.title: perf: Fix perf_pmu_migrate_context() leaving events behind
CVE-2026-99187.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

perf: Fix perf_pmu_migrate_context() leaving events behind

__perf_pmu_remove() walks the group leaders of a CPU and PMU with
perf_event_groups_for_cpu_pmu(), removing each one as it goes.
perf_remove_from_context() takes the leader out of the groups rbtree,
after which rb_next() on that node returns NULL, prematurely ending the
walk. Other groups stay behind in the source context.

On CPU hotplug, they are then torn down with the dying CPU. They keep
running until teardown, while the PMU's interrupt and migrated events
are on a new CPU, which drivers rely on never happening.

Walk ctx->event_list instead and pick out the PMU's events by their
pmu_ctx.

cifs_ses_get_chan_index(), which dereferences server->terminate; if
the put was the final reference, TCP_Server_Info is already freed and
this is a use-after-free. Same put-then-use pattern as the recently
fixed sibling in commit 717e0a25036b ("cifs: Fix server use-after-free
in cifs_chan_skip_or_disable()").

Move the put last, but do not read chan->server after dropping
chan_lock: chan points into ses->chans[], and once chan_count is
decremented a concurrent add_channel can reuse the slot and overwrite
the pointer, so the put would act on the new channel's server. Cache
the pointer under chan_lock, clear the reconnect bit and decrement
chan_count while still holding the reference, and release it after
the unlock.

CVE-2026-99590.title: ceph: clamp the inline data length in ceph_fill_inline_data()
CVE-2026-99590.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: clamp the inline data length in ceph_fill_inline_data()

The MDS decides how much inline data to attach to a reply, and the
client parses inline_len without any upper bound: ceph_decode_need()
only verifies that the message actually carries that many bytes.
ceph_fill_inline_data() then copies the data into a single folio
with no length check, so a malicious or buggy MDS returning more
inline data than the folio can hold writes past its end.

Clamp the length to folio_size() so both callers, handle_cap_grant()
and fill_inode(), are covered.

CVE-2026-99716.title: hwmon: (coretemp) Set nr_cores only after core_data allocation succeeds
CVE-2026-99716.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

hwmon: (coretemp) Set nr_cores only after core_data allocation succeeds

In init_temp_data(), pdata->nr_cores is populated from
topology_num_cores_per_package() before allocating pdata->core_data. If
that allocation fails, init_temp_data() returns NULL with
pdata->core_data still NULL and pdata->nr_cores set to a positive value.

coretemp_add_core() logs the error without failing coretemp_cpu_online(),
so the CPU still comes online with pdata->hwmon_dev registered. When the
CPU is later taken offline (or the module is unloaded),
coretemp_cpu_offline() calls get_temp_data(pd, cpu), which loops up to
pdata->nr_cores and dereferences the NULL pdata->core_data pointer.

Store the core count in a local variable and assign pdata->nr_cores only
after pdata->core_data is allocated, preserving the invariant that
pdata->nr_cores is zero whenever pdata->core_data is NULL.
